title: The Himalaya without the trek
standfirst: Mountain scale at altitudes the body can handle, if the route is chosen with some care.

blocks.heading: Fly in, walk short, sleep low
paras: Most people assume Nepal means two weeks of walking. It does not have to. The country's best views are reachable by a short flight and a two-hour walk, and the lodges at the end of them are serious.
We build the trip around sleeping altitude rather than walking distance, which keeps the days enjoyable and the nights comfortable.

blocks.heading: The valley, then the hills
blocks.caption: Mountain lodges reached in a morning rather than a week.
paras: Kathmandu deserves two nights and no more on a first trip. The temple squares are best at six in the morning, before the city wakes.
From there a short flight puts you in the hills, where the lodges are small, the walking is optional and the mountain is in front of you at breakfast.

blocks.heading: The Terai, which everyone skips
blocks.caption: Jungle camps in the lowlands, a short flight south.
paras: The lowland parks hold rhino, elephant and the occasional tiger, and almost nobody building a Nepal itinerary thinks to include them.
Three nights in the Terai changes the shape of the trip, adds warmth after the hills, and breaks the journey before the flight home.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: October and November, without question. March and April bring rhododendron and warmer valleys but more haze.

items.q: Do we need to be fit?
a: For the itineraries we build, no. Walks are two to three hours on good paths, and anything harder is optional rather than structural.
Mountain flights are weather-dependent and we plan around that. We hold a helicopter option and we never schedule a tight international connection on the day of a mountain flight.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
